title: ONNX-EdgeIDS: A Lightweight Two-Stage Edge Serving Toolkit for Network Intrusion Detection
description:
ONNX-EdgeIDS is research software for deploying machine-learning network intrusion detection on resource-constrained edge devices. It provides Kafka and ZeroMQ replay for CICIDS2017-derived flow records, a first-stage anomaly gate that filters high-volume traffic, and a second-stage tree-ensemble classifier served by ONNX Runtime or by a dependency-minimal NumPy engine exported from the same ONNX graph, together with a release gate that checks the two runtimes agree before deployment.

This release makes a failing gate say where to look. The boundary probes are built one per split node, so the failing probes name a scope (one threshold, one or two features, or global), and walking the NumPy artifact and the graph side by side on those probes reports the first node where they part and why: a threshold, the scaler of a feature, a split feature, a split mode, a leaf weight or a base value. If the artifact matches the graph there, the fault lies in the engine's arithmetic rather than in the export. The gate also gains --tie-band, which reports a label difference at an exact score tie as indeterminate rather than as a failure, since the label of a tie depends on summation order, which ONNX Runtime varies with its thread count. The research/ directory carries the experiment code and result files behind the accompanying papers, including the fault-localization experiment.
